title: Horizon and Landfall
premise: Emrys Iversen has spent a decade outrunning his mother's shadow—Dr. Halvard Iversen, the celebrated archaeologist whose expeditions he quietly made possible and whose approval he never earned. When her river expedition goes silent above the monsoon line, Emrys is the only guide willing to go up, and what he finds is not disaster but a discovery: a pre-colonial river city whose records prove a massacre was ordered by the very institution funding the dig. His mother wants to publish; the funders want the site buried with everyone who saw it. To bring the surviving team home before landfall, Emrys must smuggle them—and the evidence—downriver while deciding whether loyalty to his mother matters more than the truth she's willing to die for. He gets them out, but only by letting the river take the site itself, publishing nothing and everything at once: the truth survives in copies scattered among people the institution can never reach.
about_author: Ines Zhou is a former river pilot turned novelist who spent six seasons working supply runs on monsoon-fed waterways in Southeast Asia. Her fiction draws on that life, pairing unglamorous logistics with moral weather that changes faster than any forecast.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Emrys Iversen, drifting between salvage jobs on the lower river, refuses a charter north because it passes through territory tied to his estranged mother. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: restless avoidance—the cost of stopping made flesh.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: A fixer named Suriya tracks Emrys down: Dr. Halvard Iversen's expedition missed two scheduled check-ins above the Khet Gorge. The funding institute wants discretion. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obligation—he can't pretend not to have heard.

chapters.title: Charter Terms
chapters.summary: Emrys negotiates passage with boat captain Ondine Rask, demanding no questions about cargo or passengers. The institute sends an observer, Pell Wexler, whose politeness doesn't hide his authority. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed under pressure.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The ascent through narrowing gorges; Ondine reads water like scripture while Wexler probes Emrys about his mother. Flashbacks to childhood digs. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened by geography.

chapters.title: First Sign
chapters.summary: They find the expedition's supply cache looted but not by locals—a staged scene. Fresh tire tracks impossible this far upriver. Someone else came looking first. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the search turns from rescue to something more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Gorge Crossing
chapters.summary: Rising water forces a brutal portage; Wexler reveals the institute's real interest in speed. Emrys catches him radioing ahead in code. POV: alternating Emrys/Ondine. Emotional beat: trust fraying—everyone aboard is keeping something back.

chapters.title: Camp of the Living
chapters.summary: They find the base camp intact but half-abandoned: Halvard alive, three team members dead of 'fever,' the rest moved inland to the site. Halvard greets Emrys without surprise. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: reunion as confrontation—ten years of silence in one look.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Halvard shows Emrys the find: a buried administrative quarter with sealed records naming the institute's founders in a century-old massacre cover-up. She intends to publish before landfall strands them. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: conviction burning bright and slightly mad.

chapters.title: The Fever That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Emrys examines the dead men's effects—no fever, evidence of violence. One graduate student, Nia Okonkwo, admits she helped stage it to protect the others from the institute's advance man already in-country. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: guilt and fear braided together.

chapters.title: Landfall Warning
chapters.summary: Monsoon tracking shifts; they have nine days before the river becomes impassable and the lowlands flood. Wexler proposes evacuating everyone immediately—leaving the records 'for a proper recovery team.' POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the trap visible now, dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Mother's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Halvard calculates she can't move both her people and the archive in time. She asks Emrys to take the team down and let her stay. He refuses to choose between her survival and her truth. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Second Boat
chapters.summary: Ondine reveals she was hired months ago by someone inside the institute expecting exactly this outcome—she shows Emrys the contract. Her price for switching sides: passage out for her own reasons. POV: Ondine. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as transaction, then chosen as something more.

chapters.title: Split Cargo
chapters.summary: The plan: duplicate the records, send one set downriver hidden with the wounded, keep the originals moving overland with Halvard. Nia and Wexler each suspect the other. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: fragile conspiracy assembled from strangers.

chapters.title: Wexler's Move
chapters.summary: Wexler seizes the radio and orders an institute extraction team to the gorge, claiming mutiny. Emrys disables the boat rather than let it carry word downstream. POV: Wexler. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized—he genuinely believes he's preventing chaos.

chapters.title: Overland
chapters.summary: The overland party fights through leech country and abandoned logging roads toward a mission station with a working transmitter. Halvard's health fails; Emrys carries her pack and her argument. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: reconciliation built through shared labor, not words.

chapters.title: The Mission Station
chapters.summary: At the station they transmit copies of the records to archives, journalists, and descendant communities across three continents—truth as distributed cargo no one can sink. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost; she collapses mid-transmission.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits. The river rises twenty feet in a day. The downriver group, ambushed at the gorge, escapes only because Ondine runs rapids no sane pilot would attempt, drowning the pursuit boat. POV: Ondine. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into mastery.

chapters.title: What the Water Takes
chapters.summary: Regrouping at the delta, they learn the flood has swallowed the site whole—the physical evidence gone, the originals lost with Halvard's overland route cut off. Everything now rests on the transmissions. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief and release intertwined.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In the delta town, survivors give statements to a journalist Nia trusted. Wexler, stranded and defeated, chooses to corroborate rather than deny—his institution disowned him first. POV: Wexler. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, given freely by a broken insider.

chapters.title: Halvard
chapters.summary: Rescue teams find Halvard alive but broken-handed, carried out by villagers who read the transmitted records and claimed her as their own historian. Mother and son meet without either apologizing. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: forgiveness that doesn't require forgetting.

chapters.title: Depositions
chapters.summary: Months later: hearings begin, descendants testify, the institute dissolves its founding endowment. Emrys declines every offer to lead new expeditions. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet vindication—he stopped running by choosing where to stand.

chapters.title: Horizon and Landfall
chapters.summary: Emrys takes a small charter job upriver—not fleeing, just going—with Ondine at the helm and Nia mapping the drowned valley for the descendant communities. The site is gone; the story isn't. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: arrival at last—stopping costs less than it used to.
